Artifice

AR-tuh-fis -- from Latin ars/artis ('skill, art') + facere ('to make'). · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Artifice is clever trickery or deception, or a specific deceptive device or stratagem.

The 'antique' vase on display turned out to be an artifice: a modern reproduction carefully aged with tea stains and sandpaper.

Worked Example

The haunted house's scares depended entirely on cheap artifice -- fishing line, a fog machine, and a few well-timed hidden speakers -- rather than anything supernatural.

Notice artifice can name one specific trick or contrivance, and it isn't always sinister -- a magician's or a set designer's artifice can be a clever, even admirable, piece of craft. Compare Guile, which names a person's ongoing cunning trait, not a specific device.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

ploy: A ploy is a single calculated move made to gain an advantage over someone -- faking an injury to slow the game down. Artifice puts its weight on the cleverness of the trick or device itself, and a piece of artifice can even be admired as pure skillful craft.

gimmick: A gimmick is a flashy hook meant to grab quick attention -- a talking mascot, a spinning sign -- and the word sneers a little: there is no real substance behind it. Artifice is the opposite kind of trick: real skill and careful craft go into the deception itself.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

candor: open and honest expression, without any trickery

simplicity: the quality of being plain, direct, and without hidden tricks

Where it sits · how elaborate and calculated the scheme is — ruse → artifice → contrivance

ruse vs. artifice: A ruse is milder than artifice: a fake parking ticket taped to a windshield is one harmless trick, while artifice suggests deeper, more calculated deception.

contrivance vs. artifice: A contrivance goes further than artifice: artifice can live in a single clever trick, while a contrivance is a whole engineered apparatus -- hidden mirrors, false doors, timed pulleys -- built to carry the deception.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — arti-

root — arti-: skill, craft (Latin ars, artis; the -i- is the Latin linking vowel)

root — -fice

root — -fice: making, doing (Latin (facere, 'to make'))

Put it together

Put it together: Artifice literally means 'skill-making' -- arti- (skill, craft, from Latin ars) + -fice (making, doing, from Latin facere). Originally it just meant clever craftsmanship, which is why it can still describe an admirable trick, like a magician's, and not only a dishonest one.

Use the root in a new word: beneficial

Use the root in a new word: beneficial: Regular exercise is beneficial for both the body and the mind, doctors often remind their patients.

Word Choice

Artifice names a specific clever trick, device, or piece of craft -- and isn't always dishonest; a magician's or set designer's artifice can be admired. Compare Guile, which names an ongoing personal trait of cunning used to deceive, not a specific object or maneuver. Someone with guile might use several pieces of artifice over time.
